I visited this shop with my female dog two days ago (Wednesday) to buy some food. While I was there, I noticed that they also offered nail trimming and hair trimming around the paws, so I decided to use this service for my dog.

Since that day, my dog has been unable to walk properly, has barely been moving around, and has not been jumping at all. I became very concerned and took her to the vet today for an examination.

The vet found that my dog had strained muscles/tendons in both legs and explained that this could have been caused by excessive pulling or pressure being applied to her legs, potentially while her nails were being trimmed. This has left me extremely upset and concerned about how my dog was handled.

I find this behaviour completely unacceptable. I strongly recommend that pet owners think carefully before leaving their pets for a service where they cannot see how their animal is being handled. I would not want anyone else to go through the stress and worry that I have experienced.

I couldn’t recommend more! The staff are always so friendly, and my pooch (Bonnie) always looks lovely after a groom. They also cleaned her teeth the last time we went in and they looked so fantastic afterwards!
Absolutely ridiculous signs blind residents and neighbours at night.
Friendly and efficient service, we were delighted with our cavapoo’s groom!

We visit Pet Pavilion in Chiswick weekly. My Pugy loves to visit this store. There’s a great range of products, helpful staff. Angela is very knowledgeable on products. Thank you for great customer service
Lovely ladies and good selection of products.
Very nice store! Lots of high-quality dog ​​toys (made in the UK). Nice staff!

Absolutely unacceptable.

The digital screens outside Pet Pavilion in Chiswick are blindingly bright, especially at night. This photo was taken in the evening, yet the glare is so intense it completely dominates the surrounding area. It’s genuinely distracting and, in my opinion, poses a real hazard for drivers on the road.

There’s a clear responsibility for businesses to ensure their signage doesn’t interfere with road safety, and this goes far beyond what would be considered reasonable brightness. It’s not just unpleasant — it’s dangerous.

If an accident were to occur due to drivers being dazzled, I wouldn’t be surprised if serious questions were asked about liability.

This needs addressing urgently. Dim the screens at night or install proper brightness controls — because in its current state, it’s completely inappropriate for a public roadside setting.
